chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Alawi from al-Amraki from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) said:
I asked him about a female slave owned jointly by two men, one of whom married her off while the other was absent. He said: 'If the absent partner dislikes it, the marriage is not valid.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying a co-owned female slave if one partner is absent?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim clarifies the condition of consent in the marriage of a co-owned female slave, emphasizing that the absent partner's veto power invalidates the union if he objects. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that ownership shares confer equal rights in marital decisions, ensuring that the absence of one owner does not override his preference. This ruling underscores the importance of mutual agreement in family law to prevent disputes among co-owners.
